definition: Microsoft Bot Framework provides tools and interfaces for building conversational applications and connecting them to supported channels.
example: A developer connects a support bot to a messaging channel and routes inquiries to its dialog logic.

definition: Microsoft Digital Image Suite was a consumer application suite for editing, organizing and sharing photographs.
example: A user adjusted color in a scanned photograph and sorted it into an album.

definition: Microsoft Forms creates online questionnaires, quizzes and polls and collects responses.
example: A teacher creates a quiz that records students' answers in a response summary.

definition: Microsoft HoloLens is a wearable mixed-reality device that presents digital content registered in the wearer's surroundings.
example: A trainee views an overlay identifying parts of a machine.

definition: Microsoft Intune is a cloud service for managing organizational devices, applications and related compliance policies.
example: An administrator checks whether enrolled laptops meet disk-encryption requirements.

definition: A Microsoft Language Interface Pack provides localized interface text for supported software, sometimes requiring a base language installation.
example: A user installs and selects a display language to read supported menus in that language.
sense_note: Specific coverage varies by product and package.

definition: Microsoft Lists is a Microsoft 365 tool for tracking structured records in configurable lists and views.
example: A team creates an equipment issue list with filters for department and status.

definition: Microsoft Lync was a business communication application for instant messaging, presence, calling and meetings.
example: A user checked a colleague's presence before starting an online call.

definition: Microsoft Paint is a basic raster graphics editor for drawing and editing images.
example: A user crops a screenshot and adds colored labels.

definition: Microsoft Sentinel is a cloud security platform for collecting, analyzing and responding to security event data.
example: A defender investigates an alert by reviewing related sign-in and system logs.

definition: Microsoft Teams live events refers to a Teams broadcast format in which designated presenters and producers deliver an event to viewers.
example: A producer manages presenters and moderated questions during an organization-wide broadcast.
sense_note: The label is feature-specific; do not infer availability or equate it to every Teams broadcast format.

definition: Microsoft Teams Phone adds telephony and call-control capabilities to Teams, with external calling through configured connectivity.
example: An organization routes calls for a main number to a queue in Teams.

definition: Microsoft Transaction Server was a Microsoft platform for running distributed components with services such as transaction coordination and resource management.
example: An enterprise application used it to coordinate a business operation across transactional resources.

definition: Microsoft Visio is software for creating diagrams such as flowcharts, floor plans and network maps.
example: A process analyst uses Visio to document who approves each step of an invoice workflow.

definition: Microsoft Works was a consumer productivity suite offering basic document, spreadsheet and database functions.
example: A household used its spreadsheet component to track shared expenses.

definition: MicroStation is computer-aided design software for creating and documenting two- and three-dimensional designs.
example: An engineer drafts a roadway plan and attaches reference drawings.

definition: MicroStrategy Desktop refers to a desktop business intelligence application for exploring data and building visual analyses.
example: An analyst builds a dashboard from a sales spreadsheet.
sense_note: The product name has varied across releases; confirm the version before describing server integration.

definition: MicroStrategy Intelligence Server is the server tier that executes and distributes MicroStrategy analytics and manages associated queries and services.
example: A report request is processed by the server and returned to a browser client.

definition: MicroStrategy Office is a Microsoft Office integration for accessing and using MicroStrategy reports or data in Office documents.
example: A finance analyst refreshes a report embedded in an Excel workbook.

definition: MicroStrategy OLAP Services provides in-memory analytical processing for manipulating report views without issuing every query to the underlying data source.
example: An analyst changes filters on a cached dataset to compare sales regions.

definition: MicroStrategy Report Services refers to functionality for designing formatted analytical documents and reports.
example: A team creates a paginated operating report with tables and charts.

definition: The MicroStrategy Software Development Kit provides programming interfaces and development resources for extending or embedding MicroStrategy features.
example: A developer integrates a governed analytics view into an internal application.

definition: MicroStrategy Transaction Services supports data-entry and write-back workflows from analytics interfaces to configured data sources.
example: A manager submits a revised forecast value from a dashboard control.

definition: MicroStrategy Visual Insight was a visual data-discovery tool for building interactive analyses and dashboards.
example: An analyst drags fields into a chart to explore revenue differences across regions.

definition: MicroStrategy Web is a browser interface for accessing reports, dashboards and related business intelligence tools.
example: A manager opens a shared dashboard in a browser and filters it to their region.

definition: MIKE URBAN is modeling software for urban water infrastructure such as water supply, drainage and sewer networks.
example: A civil engineer simulates how heavy rainfall affects flows through a stormwater network.

definition: Military standards and specifications prescribe requirements for materials, equipment, services or processes in military acquisition and operation.
example: A procurement specialist checks whether a supplier's test evidence satisfies a contractually referenced specification.

definition: Mind mapping organizes related ideas visually around a central topic using branching associations.
example: A team maps possible causes of delivery delays around a central problem.

definition: MITRE ATT&CK is a knowledge base and framework that organizes observed adversary behavior into tactics and techniques for security analysis.
example: A defender maps known security alerts to ATT&CK categories to identify gaps in monitoring.

definition: Mobile application design plans an application's functionality, interactions and presentation for mobile devices and contexts.
example: A designer maps how a commuter would complete a ticket purchase with one hand.

definition: Mobile UI design creates the visual and interactive controls through which users operate a mobile application.
example: A designer chooses button sizes and spacing that make a form easy to tap.

definition: Mobile UX design improves how users accomplish goals in mobile contexts by addressing workflows, usability and accessibility.
example: A researcher observes people using an app on a crowded platform and identifies where the process breaks down.

definition: ModelOps coordinates the deployment, monitoring, governance and maintenance of analytical models across their operational lifecycle.
example: A model owner tracks production versions and triggers review when validation metrics decline.

definition: ModelSim is an electronic design simulation tool for testing hardware description language models.
example: An engineer uses a testbench to verify a counter's expected sequence in a simulation.

definition: Modern methods of construction describe approaches that improve building production through techniques such as off-site manufacture or standardized assemblies.
example: A builder installs factory-made wall panels to reduce on-site assembly time.
sense_note: This is an umbrella term; qualifying methods vary across programs.

definition: MODO is a three-dimensional content-creation application for modeling, texturing, rendering and animation.
example: An artist models a product, applies materials and renders a studio image.

definition: Moist heat sterilization uses controlled moist heat to inactivate microorganisms, including resistant forms, in compatible materials.
example: A facility uses a validated steam sterilization cycle for compatible instruments.

definition: Mold setting installs, aligns and prepares a mold in manufacturing equipment for a production run.
example: An operator secures a replacement mold and verifies its alignment before production.

definition: Molding forms a material into a defined shape using a mold or cavity.
example: A manufacturer forms plastic housings in a mold that defines their dimensions.
sense_note: This is a general manufacturing sense; distinguish casting, injection molding and architectural moldings where needed.

definition: Moldings installation and maintenance fit, secure, finish and repair decorative or protective trim on surfaces.
example: A carpenter cuts and fits replacement trim around a damaged doorway.
